title: Laboratory Skills and Safety
summary: This lesson teaches essential laboratory techniques, safety rules, and proper data recording methods. Students will learn how to work safely and accurately in a biology lab.

sections.heading: Basic Lab Techniques
sections.body:
Learn how to handle common lab equipment such as pipettes, microscopes, and test tubes. Always label your samples clearly and use the correct volume when measuring liquids. Practice proper pipetting: press the plunger to the first stop, immerse the tip, and release slowly to avoid bubbles.

When using a microscope, start with the lowest magnification to locate the specimen, then switch to higher powers for detail. Clean lenses with lens paper and never touch the glass with your fingers.

sections.heading: Safety Rules
sections.body:
Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) at all times: lab coat, safety goggles, and closed-toe shoes. Know the location of safety equipment such as fire extinguishers, eyewash stations, and first‑aid kits.

Never eat, drink, or chew gum in the lab. If a spill occurs, alert the instructor, contain the area, and follow the proper cleanup procedure for the material involved.

sections.heading: Accurate Data Recording
sections.body:
Record observations immediately in a lab notebook, using clear headings, dates, and experiment titles. Include details such as sample names, measurements, and any unexpected results.

Use tables and graphs to organize data. When drawing conclusions, refer directly to the recorded numbers rather than memory.

sections.heading: Example: Simple Enzyme Assay
sections.body:
In this short experiment, students measure the rate at which an enzyme breaks down a substrate. Steps: 1) Label three test tubes (control, low enzyme, high enzyme). 2) Add equal volumes of substrate to each tube. 3) Add the appropriate amount of enzyme, start a timer, and record the color change every 30 seconds.

Safety tip: Wear gloves when handling the enzyme, and dispose of all solutions in the designated biohazard container.

key_terms.meaning: Clothing and gear that protect the wearer from hazards, such as lab coats, goggles, and gloves.
A tool used to measure and transfer very small volumes of liquid, typically 0.1–1000 µL.
A sample that is not exposed to the experimental variable, used for comparison.
Materials contaminated with biological agents that must be disposed of in special containers.
A structured arrangement of numbers and observations that makes it easy to compare results.
A written set of step‑by‑step instructions to ensure consistent and safe lab practices.

quiz.q: Which piece of PPE is essential when using a microscope?
quiz.why: Safety goggles protect the eyes from accidental splashes or debris.

quiz.q: What should you do first if a chemical spill occurs?
options: Alert the instructor and contain the area
Ignore it if it looks small
quiz.why: Alerting the instructor ensures proper containment and cleanup.

quiz.q: Why is it important to record data during an experiment rather than after it ends?
quiz.why: Recording immediately prevents forgetting details and reduces errors.

quiz.q: In an enzyme assay, the control tube contains:
quiz.why: The control has substrate but no enzyme, showing the baseline reaction.

steps.label: Press First Stop
steps.text: Press the plunger to the first stop before immersing the tip.

steps.label: Immerse Tip
steps.text: Place the tip just below the liquid surface.

steps.label: Release Slowly
steps.text: Release the plunger slowly to draw liquid without bubbles.

steps.label: Dispense
steps.text: Press to the second stop to dispense the exact volume.

steps.label: Low Power Scan
steps.text: Start with the lowest magnification to locate the specimen.

steps.label: Center Specimen
steps.text: Center the object using the stage controls.

steps.label: Increase Magnification
steps.text: Switch to higher powers for detailed view.

steps.label: Clean Lenses
steps.text: Wipe lenses with lens paper; never touch glass with fingers.

items.name: High Enzyme Tube
